questions.prompt: Primarily encountered by modern readers as inert written texts, the vernacular riddles of early medieval England contain 'implicit vestiges' of an interactive performance context, scholar Jill Frederick argues. Locative phrases scattered throughout the riddles indicate the space shared by their speakers and audiences; the common refrain 'say what I am called' invites a verbalized response; and the conflation of many of the riddles' speakers with their solutions suggests a form of dramatic impersonation perhaps meant to entertain during public gatherings.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.A: It is reasonable to conclude based on textual evidence from the vernacular riddles of early medieval England that they were mainly performed at large public gatherings, though documentation is unlikely to exist.
options.B: Linguistic evidence found within the vernacular riddles of early medieval England suggests that they may have been intended to be performed in communal settings, though this isn't how they are generally experienced by readers today.
options.C: People of early medieval England likely found that era's vernacular riddles to be more amusing than modern readers do.
options.D: Scholars once assumed that the vernacular riddles were originally intended to be read silently, but newly uncovered historical documents corroborate that they were for oral performance.

options.B: "No moment for this talk, / Lest he discern my coming, and I lose / The scheme, wherewith I think to catch him soon."
options.C: "Go near now silently, and make me know / If still he persevere, and hold this spot, / Or have roamed elsewhere..."

questions.prompt: Cover crops, such as teff, are planted by many farmers between main growing seasons. questions.prompt:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• NASA mission STS-134 took place from May 16, 2011, to June 1, 2011.
• Astronauts Andrew Feustel and Michael Fincke were crew members of STS-134.
• May 22, 2011: Feustel and Fincke performed an extravehicular activity (EVA) to refill space station radiators with ammonia.
• An EVA is an activity done by astronauts outside the spacecraft.
• The duration of their EVA was 8 hours and 7 minutes.
• Theirs is counted among the longest completed spacewalks to date.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize the duration of Feustel and Fincke's EVA. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: During their time as crew members of STS-134, Feustel and Fincke completed an EVA.
options.B: Lasting 8 hours and 7 minutes, Feustel and Fincke's EVA is one of the longest spacewalks completed to date.
options.C: Feustel and Fincke completed an EVA, also known as a spacewalk, in which they left the spacecraft to refill radiators.
options.D: The EVA completed by STS-134 crewmembers Feustel and Fincke took place from May 16, 2011, to June 1, 2011.

questions.prompt:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Waiting is a 1987 black-and-white linocut print by Kuwaiti artist Thuraya Al-Baqsami.
• It depicts a tranquil, everyday scene (a woman in a headscarf looking out a window).
• ¡Será toda nuestra! ('It will all be ours!') is a 1977 color linocut print by Mexican American artist Carlos Cortéz.
• It features a scene with an explicitly political point of view (a group of laborers preparing to go on strike).
• Relief printing is a technique in which an image is carved onto a printing block, covered in ink, and stamped onto paper.
• Linocut is a type of relief printing that uses linoleum tile as the printing block.
questions.question: The student wants to contrast the subject matter of the two prints. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Cortéz made ¡Será toda nuestra! in 1977, while Al-Baqsami made Waiting later, in 1987.
options.B: The scenes depicted in both works were first carved onto a printing block, then stamped onto paper; however, one work is a linocut, while the other is a relief print.
options.C: Cortéz's print expresses an explicitly political point of view, while Al-Baqsami's depicts a tranquil, everyday scene.
options.D: The print by Cortéz is a color linocut; by contrast, Al-Baqsami's is a relief print.

questions.prompt:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) is a method of spreading crushed basalt on farmland to capture carbon dioxide (CO2) and improve soil health.
• ERW increases crop yields and removes harmful CO2 from the air.
• ERW offers a low-cost, low-tech alternative to expensive, energy-intensive carbon capture methods.
• The CO2 captured by ERW becomes stable bicarbonate in soil water, which eventually streams into the ocean to remain safely stored for hundreds of years.
• ERW can improve rural economies by reducing farmers' need for fertilizers and increasing their earnings from carbon credits.
questions.question: The student wants to explain why ERW is a superior method for capturing CO2. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: ERW improves soil health and helps farmers increase their income from selling carbon credits.
options.B: ERW is a method of spreading crushed basalt on farmland to capture CO2, improving rural economies.
options.C: ERW removes CO2 from the air in a way that is both low-cost and low-tech.
options.D: The CO2 captured by ERW becomes stable bicarbonate, which improves soil health by remaining in the ocean for hundreds of years.
